ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the line $l_1: y=kx+4$ intersects with the line $l_2: y=ax+b$ at point $P(4, m)$. What is the solution set of the inequality $kx+4 \ge ax+b$ with respect to $x$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} To solve: for the line $l_{1}: y=kx+4$ and the line $l_{2}: y=ax+b$ intersect at point $P(4, m)$,\\
to satisfy the inequality $kx+4\ge ax+b$,\\
the graph of $l_{1}: y=kx+4$ must be above that of $l_{2}: y=ax+b$,\\
from the graph, it is known to intersect at point $P(4, m)$,\\
with the x-coordinate being 4,\\
hence, the solution set for the inequality $kx+4\ge ax+b$ is: $\boxed{x\ge 4}$.
